item.title: Building in Travel Has Never Mattered More
item.description: Travel is where history gets physical. We're in it. Right where we should be.

item.title: Air India Scouts for New CEO: Reports
item.description: Air India’s next chief won’t be fixing an airline that’s broken, the CEO will be steadying one that’s fragile in quieter ways. This is now about execution. And for Tatas, the hire could speed up India’s aviation rise, or turn it into a longer, far more expensive journey.

item.title: The Case for Travel Flow Corridors: A Framework for Reciprocal Tourism
item.description: Live tourism creates temporary tourism corridors, but the real opportunity is permanent infrastructure — aviation networks, visa liberalization, and booking platforms — that enables circulation whether or not Taylor Swift is on tour.

item.title: Ryanair vs. Wizz Air: Who Flew Higher Over the Holidays?
item.description: Wizz Air’s year-on-year surge looks impressive, but Ryanair’s fuller planes and steadier execution still set the benchmark.

item.title: Cruise Sector and U.S. Government Block Hawaii’s Climate Tax on Cruise Ships
item.description: As more destinations consider climate-linked tourism fees, Hawaii’s legal battle could set a national precedent.

item.title: Aman’s Secret Third Hotel Brand? These Signs Point to ‘Atma’
item.description: Aman appears to be working on a third ultra-luxury hotel brand, Atma. The first U.S. hotel may have 185 suites, an unusually high room count for the group. Here's what Skift found by sleuthing.

item.title: Trump Administration Dials Back Airline Enforcement, Seeks Fewer Fines
item.description: After pulling back several Biden-era rules on airline consumer protection, the Trump administration says it will take a far more conservative approach to enforcement — expect fewer rules and fines for airlines.

item.title: Hilton Blames Franchisee After DHS Blasts it for Refusing Service
item.description: DHS has accused a Minneapolis Hilton franchisee of canceling ICE agent reservations. Hilton's corporate headquarters says the incident doesn't reflect its values.

item.title: Ryanair Contract With OTAs Reveals Fees and Restrictions — Scoop
item.description: The integration charges are more than minor annoyances for smaller OTAs. And the cumbersome way the Ryanair pop-ups work, plus the lack of promotional fares, make the OTAs second-class flight sellers.

item.title: How Indians Are Turning Travel Into a Luxury Buying Strategy. Plus, A Silent Year-End IPO Filing
item.description: Indians love shopping and a good bargain. With airlines, destinations, and travel players offering affordable access to travel, Indians are not shying away from crossing borders just to get their hands on luxury products at cheaper prices.
